allocatable array with a count and move_alloc growth

No push_back; the pattern above is the idiom, because the language itself has no container type.

std::unique_ptr

allocatable

Sole ownership, automatic release and a deep copy on assignment are the default behavior of an allocatable.

std::shared_ptr, a raw pointer

pointer

Aliasing and manual release.

NumPy a = np.zeros (n); a = np.append (a, v)

allocate (a(n), source=0.0_dp); a = [a, v]

Same cost as np.append: a new array on every call.

MATLAB x(end+1) = v

x = [x, v]

Same: the array is copied; MATLAB hides it.

Java and Python object references

class(t), allocatable, or a pointer to share

Assignment of an allocatable copies the object, including its allocatable components; two names for one object need a pointer.

See Fortran for Programmers of Other Languages for the full comparison.

Compiler support and diagnostics

The following was verified on 2026-10-18 with the examples on this page; the "not verified" family names mean that no compiler of that family was available.

Feature GNU Fortran 16.2 LLVM Flang 23

allocate and deallocate with stat=, fixed-length errmsg=, source=, mold= and a type-spec

Accepted; all examples built warning-free with -std=f2023 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -fcheck=all.

Accepted, with different stat codes and message texts.

Reallocation on assignment, including bounds from lbound (expr) and deferred-length character

Yes, on by default (-frealloc-lhs); -Wrealloc-lhs and -Wrealloc-lhs-all report it.

Yes.

Terminates with a message.

In the test for this page the program ran on with exit status 0 and no message.

errmsg= with a deferred-length allocatable character (F2023)

Compiles with a warning; crashes with SIGSEGV when an error occurs.

Compiles; the message is not stored and the variable stays unallocated.

Rejected: "Rank mismatch in array reference" and "Array index must be scalar".

Rejected: "Must be a scalar value, but is a rank-1 array".

Accepted.

Accepted; the positional form call move_alloc (a, b, stat, msg) caused an internal compiler error.

Accepted in both forms.

Yes.

Yes.

Yes; see the table of options above.

Not available in the version tested (-fbounds-check is rejected).

Not verified here, because no compiler for them is installed: Intel ifx, NAG, HPE Cray and NVIDIA HPC compilers. See History, Standards and Compilers for the per-compiler support table of the other Fortran 2023 features, and Compilers and Compiler Options for the options.

Standard-version provenance

Feature Standard Notes

allocatable arrays (local and module variables), allocate, deallocate, allocated, stat=, zero-sized allocation

Fortran 90

The first form of dynamic memory in standard Fortran; pointer arrays arrived at the same time.

Automatic deallocation of local allocatable arrays on return

Fortran 95

In Fortran 90 their status after return was not defined, which made them unreliable in procedures.

Allocatable dummy arguments, function results and components (the technical report ISO/IEC TR 15581)

Fortran 2003

Incorporated into the standard in Fortran 2003, with allocatable scalars.

Reallocation on assignment, move_alloc, source=, errmsg=, deferred-length character, polymorphic allocatables

Fortran 2003

-std=f95 in GNU Fortran turns reallocation off.

mold= in allocate, recursive allocatable components, allocatable coarrays

Fortran 2008

Optional stat= and errmsg= in move_alloc, simple move_alloc (when from is not a coarray)

Fortran 2018 or 2023 (the Fortran 2023 text has both)

Not in Fortran 2008.

Arrays as bounds in allocate, the rank clause, deferred-length allocatable errmsg= and iomsg=

Fortran 2023

None of the three works in GNU Fortran 16.2, and only the rank clause works in LLVM Flang 23.

Allocation of an unallocated coarray or coindexed object by assignment

Removed in Fortran 2023

It was permitted in Fortran 2008 (4.3.4 of the Fortran 2023 text) for scalar, nonpolymorphic coarrays without deferred type parameters.

Fortran 2028 (draft J3/26-007r1)

Upcoming

Not covered by this page; see What’s New and Fortran 2028 Preview.

Where the books are outdated

Modern Fortran Explained (Metcalf, Reid, Cohen and Bader, 3rd edition, Fortran 2023) covers allocatable variables, dummy arguments, results and components, allocate and deallocate, reallocation on assignment and move_alloc in its chapter 6, with the Fortran 2023 additions near the end. As a reference to the language it remains accurate. The points where a reader has to look beyond it are:

  • Compiler status. The book describes the Fortran 2023 features as part of the language and does not say which compilers implement them. As the table above shows, the array bounds in allocate and the allocation of a deferred-length errmsg do not work in GNU Fortran 16.2 or LLVM Flang 23, and the rank clause works only in Flang. Portable code writes the scalar bounds and a fixed-length message variable.

  • Compiler options and diagnostics. The book says nothing about -frealloc-lhs, -Wrealloc-lhs, -fcheck=bounds, -fstack-arrays or -fmax-stack-var-size, about the run-time messages of allocation errors, or about the fact that "Segmentation fault" on entry to a procedure with a large automatic array is a stack overflow. They are covered above.

  • Stack and heap. The book does not discuss where automatic arrays live. As the experiment above shows, the answer depends on the compiler and on its options.

  • Diagnosing leaks. The book shows that allocatables do not leak but gives no tool to find the leaks that pointers still allow; Valgrind and -fcheck=pointer are described above.

  • Appendix A. The book’s list of deprecated features is the authors' recommendation. None of what this page covers (allocate, pointer, reallocation on assignment) is obsolescent in the standard.

The fortran-lang best-practices page on allocatable arrays is current in its advice, but its resize snippet declares neither its work array tmp nor consistently spells initial_size, so it does not compile as printed; use the pattern above.

Common mistakes at a glance

Mistake Symptom Fix

allocate of an already allocated variable

"Attempting to allocate already allocated variable", or error termination

if (.not. allocated (x)) allocate (x(n)), or deallocate first, or assign x = ....

deallocate of an unallocated variable

"Attempt to DEALLOCATE unallocated", or error termination

Test with allocated, or rely on automatic deallocation.

Reading an unallocated array

Garbage, "below lower bound of" a huge number, or a crash

Allocate before use; build with -Wall -O2 (maybe-uninitialized) and -fcheck=all.

Passing an unallocated array to a non-allocatable, non-optional dummy argument

Crash inside the callee

Allocate first, or make the dummy argument optional, or allocatable.

x(:) = y with a different size

"Array bound mismatch" (or silent overrun without -fcheck=bounds)

Write x = y so the array is reallocated.

Assuming lower bound 1 after x = y

Off-by-one reads

Remember that x takes lbound (y); use x = y(:) or pass to an assumed-shape dummy argument.

label = name for a deferred-length character

Trailing blanks in the new value

label = trim (name).

x = [x, v] in a loop

Quadratic time

Capacity doubling with move_alloc.

Allocatable function result called in a loop

Repeated allocation and deallocation

Pass the output array as an intent(out) argument allocated once.

Large automatic array

"Segmentation fault" on entry to a procedure

Use an allocatable array, or raise the stack limit as a stop-gap.

Large fixed-size local array in GNU Fortran

-Wsurprising: moved from stack to static storage

Use an allocatable array.

Pointer to an allocatable without target, or move_alloc to a variable without target

Undefined pointer

Add target or avoid the pointer.

Deallocating an object while one of its parts is a dummy argument

Not allowed, no diagnostic

Deallocate from the owner after the call.

Relying on a particular stat value or message text

Works on one compiler only

Test stat /= 0.

errmsg= as a deferred-length character

Crash on GNU Fortran 16.2

Use a fixed-length variable.

Counting on a final subroutine of a main-program variable

It does not run at the end of the program

Put the variable in a block construct.
